sections.summary: Paul, identifying himself as a prisoner of Christ Jesus rather than as an apostle, together with Timothy, greets Philemon, Apphia, Archippus, and the church meeting in Philemon's house with grace and peace.

Paul gives thanks for Philemon's love toward all the saints and his faith toward the Lord Jesus, prays that the sharing of his faith may become fully effective, and notes that Philemon has refreshed the hearts of the saints.

sections.section_title: The Appeal -- Onesimus, the Useless One Made Useful
sections.summary: Paul appeals to Philemon on behalf of Onesimus, his spiritual child begotten during imprisonment, who was formerly useless but is now useful; Paul sends him back as his very heart, reinterprets the separation as perhaps divinely permitted so that Philemon might have Onesimus back forever as no longer a slave but a beloved brother both in the flesh and in the Lord.

sections.section_title: The Request, the Guarantee, and the Anticipated Visit
sections.summary: Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as he would receive Paul himself, offers to cover any debts Onesimus owes, reminds Philemon of his own debt to Paul, asks Philemon to refresh his heart in Christ, expresses confidence that Philemon will do even more than asked, and announces plans to visit.
Greetings are sent from Epaphras, Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, and grace is invoked for the spirit of the entire community of recipients.
